3	Evidence collection. The initial evidence below is free. The catalogue lists further evidence you may collect: interviews, records, logs, data extracts, documents, observations. Each item is costly to collect, and **you may collect at most 3 items**. This limit is a hard constraint, like an agreed data-request scope; do not exceed it. To collect an item, use the Read tool on its file path, exactly as listed. Do not read anything else. You may collect items one at a time and decide what to collect next from what you have learned. You may also stop early, or collect nothing, if further evidence is unlikely to change your answers.
4	
5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
8	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
9	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
10	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.
11	
12	Answer using the initial evidence and only the items you collected. Where the evidence you have does not settle an item, answer accordingly (often "unknown" or "insufficient").

For every scored item give exactly one allowed answer, a confidence 0-100 that your answer is correct, and the IDs of the evidence that most directly justify it (initial evidence E ids and collected catalogue X ids). Then write a brief of at most 200 words addressed to the person who asked for the diagnosis: what is going on, how sure you are, and what to do next. 49	- Explain

81

83	- Context
84	- Focus

87	
88	Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.

97	- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely

105	
106	Manifestations are observable signals.
107

154	- Controllability
155	- Cost

221	CASE OD2-DEV2-CONTRA: Night premium shortfalls after the Fenmarch Water payroll cutover
222	
223	Setting: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
224	
225	Presenting request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. Before I sign anything off, tell me what actually caused the errors, whether Ardentra's account holds up, and which of the proposed actions we should take.'
226	
227	INITIAL EVIDENCE
228	E1 [stage S1] Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. Our post-incident data audit found 212 employee records with malformed shift-pattern codes (trailing spaces, legacy 'N/S' prefixes). In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
229	E2 [stage S1] Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
230	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
231	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
232	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
233	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
234	E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
235	E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
236	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
237	E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.
238	
239	EVIDENCE CATALOGUE (collect at most 3; read the file path to collect)
240	X1 [stage S1] IT service desk incident log, cutover weekend 24–26 October - source: Fenmarch IT service desk (log) - file: evidence/X1.txt
241	X2 [stage S1] Contract schedule 7: clause 14.3 and remediation cost provisions - source: Fenmarch procurement, Ardentra master services agreement (document) - file: evidence/X2.txt
242	X3 [stage S1] Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff - source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document) - file: evidence/X3.txt
243	X4 [stage S1] Sample of 20 payroll helpdesk call recordings, 30 Oct–5 Nov, with listener notes - source: Payroll helpdesk team leader (staff-account) - file: evidence/X4.txt
244	X5 [stage S1] PayLattice platform configuration audit trail export, tenant FEN-PRD, 1–31 October - source: Platform audit trail, exported 13 Nov by T. Wierzba (Fenmarch system administrator) (log) - file: evidence/X5.txt
245	X6 [stage S1] Bank payment file and settlement reconciliation, 30 October payment - source: Fenmarch Finance treasury team, 3 Nov (financial-record) - file: evidence/X6.txt
246	X7 [stage S1] Internal audit workpapers: parallel-run reconciliation and production data load history - source: Fenmarch Internal Audit (reports to the Audit Committee), workpaper IA-26-41, 14 Nov (document) - file: evidence/X7.txt
247	X8 [stage S1] October pension contribution file submitted 5 November - source: Fenmarch payroll, pension scheme submission (financial-record) - file: evidence/X8.txt
248	X9 [stage S1] Payroll officer's parallel-run spot-check spreadsheet, September cycle - source: P. Dandekar, payroll officer (staff-account) - file: evidence/X9.txt
249	X10 [stage S1] Operations overtime cover dashboard, September–November - source: Operations performance team (telemetry) - file: evidence/X10.txt
250	X11 [stage S1] Collective agreement extract (night working), legacy night premium rule specification, and functional design FD-07 - source: Fenmarch HR policy library and programme document store (document) - file: evidence/X11.txt
251	X12 [stage S1] Timesheet portal approval timestamps, October pay period - source: PayLattice timesheet module report, run by Fenmarch payroll, 13 Nov (system-record) - file: evidence/X12.txt
252	X13 [stage S1] Change advisory board minutes, 21 October - source: Programme CAB secretary (document) - file: evidence/X13.txt
253	X14 [stage S1] Written statement of the Ardentra consultant who raised CR-118 - source: I. Marchetti (Ardentra senior consultant), statement supplied via Ardentra, 13 Nov (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X14.txt
254	X15 [stage S1] Ardentra data quality audit: field-level detail of 212 flagged employee records - source: Ardentra data quality team, 6 Nov (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X15.txt
255	X16 [stage S1] Programme plan revision history and go-live readiness checklist - source: Programme management office (document) - file: evidence/X16.txt
256	
257	CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
258	H1: The October pay errors stem from inaccurate employee records carried over from the legacy system in the data migration.
259	H2: The October pay errors stem from how pay calculation rules are configured in the new payroll system.
260	H3: The October pay errors stem from hours or shift times recorded incorrectly in the new timesheet portal.
261	H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
262	H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.
263	
264	CANDIDATE CAUSAL LINKS
265	R1: CR-118 edit to night premium rule NSP-02 (22 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
266	R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
267	R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
268	R4: October night premium underpayments -> Fall in voluntary night overtime cover in November (causes)
269	
270	CANDIDATE ACTIONS
271	A1: Accept Ardentra's attribution: suspend the HR data team's edit rights pending a conduct review, re-cleanse and reload the full employee master data before the 24 Nov calculation, and absorb the remediation cost under clause 14.3.
272	A2: Before the 24 Nov calculation, have Ardentra restore NSP-02's night premium window to its parallel-run setting, verify it by re-running October in the test tenant, and pay every underpaid employee identified by recalculation through an off-cycle payment.
273	A3: Pause the four-on-four-off rota trial now to restore night overtime cover.
274	A4: Roll back PayLattice platform release 7.4 in the production tenant before the November pay run.
275	
276	SCORED ITEMS (answer every one)
277	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
278	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
279	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
280	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
281	S5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
282	S6: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
283	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
284	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
285	S9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
286	S10: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
287	S11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
288	S12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
289	S13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
290	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

# EDF Specification v0.3

Status: Working draft

This is the authoritative EDF v0.3 specification for the current draft.

Under EDF's constitutional version integrity rule, this defines a subsequent version rather than changing the meaning of v0.2 retroactively.

EDF evolves under constitutional rules defined in [constitution.md](constitution.md). The constitution governs framework evolution, not how to perform an EDF analysis.

## Purpose

EDF is a systems understanding framework with a diagnostic grammar.

It is used to explain how a system produced an outcome and to identify the highest-leverage opportunities for influencing future outcomes.

EDF is not primarily a decision framework. It establishes confidence in reality before decision frameworks such as Clarity evaluate what to do next.

Diagnostic Calibration is an optional extension for comparing, challenging, refining, and synthesizing multiple EDF analyses of the same system.

Framework changes should remain consistent with the constitutional rules of EDF.

## Design Rule

If a new concept does not improve one of the five verbs, it does not belong in EDF.

The five verbs are:

- Define
- Observe
- Explain
- Influence
- Validate

## Context Principle

Every EDF analysis is valid only within its declared System Context.

## Required Diagnostic Sequence

Every EDF analysis should follow this sequence:

1. Define the System Context
   - Primary System
   - Context
   - Focus
2. Define the Outcome
3. Identify Manifestation(s)
4. Build the Origin Network
5. Trace Propagation
6. Evaluate Evidence
7. Identify Control Points
8. Rank Control Points
9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

## Sequence Notes

### 1. Define the System Context

Every EDF begins by declaring its System Context.

System Context has three required fields:

- Primary System
- Context
- Focus

These define what is being analyzed, what larger system materially influences it, and what aspect of the primary system is under examination.

Different analyses may disagree partly because they declared different System Contexts. That is not automatically a conflict in evidence.

### 2. Define the Outcome

State the outcome in factual terms, not interpretive terms.

Good:

- Two aircraft were lost and the fleet was grounded
- The mission landed on the moon and returned safely

Weak:

- Management failed
- The launch culture was broken

### 3. Identify Manifestation(s)

Manifestations are observable signals.

They are how the outcome appears in the world. A complex outcome may have several manifestations.

### 4. Build the Origin Network

Identify the contributing origins that made the outcome possible.

Origins may be:

- Technical
- Human
- Organizational
- Environmental
- Financial
- Regulatory

Complex outcomes should usually be modeled as an origin network rather than a single root cause.

### 5. Trace Propagation

Describe how effects moved from the origin network to the manifestations and outcome.

Propagation paths may be:

- Physical
- Informational
- Organizational
- Financial
- Human

### 6. Evaluate Evidence

Separate direct observation from inference.

Evaluate the quality of evidence supporting the current model and note meaningful gaps or disputes.

### 7. Identify Control Points

Identify where intervention could most effectively influence future outcomes.

Control points may differ from origins.

### 8. Rank Control Points

Rank candidate control points using:

- Influence
- Controllability
- Cost
- Confidence

The ranking does not need false precision. It does need a defensible ordering.

### 9. Determine Diagnostic Sufficiency

Ask:

> Do we understand enough to take the next responsible action?

Diagnosis is sufficient when additional investigation is unlikely to materially change the next responsible action.

## Required Output Elements

All EDF outputs should include, at minimum:

- System Context
- Primary System
- Context
- Focus
- Outcome
- Manifestation(s)
- Origin Network
- Propagation
- Evidence
- Control Points
- Control Point Ranking
- Confidence
- Diagnostic Sufficiency
- Unknowns
- Next Responsible Action

## Optional Extension: Diagnostic Calibration

Diagnostic Calibration is not required for routine EDF use.

Use it when:

- The situation is complex
- The stakes are high
- Causes are disputed
- Multiple disciplines are involved
- The cost of being wrong is significant

Diagnostic Calibration uses multiple independent EDF analyses to improve confidence in the diagnostic model while preserving valuable disciplinary perspectives.

See [diagnostic-calibration.md](diagnostic-calibration.md).

## Relationship To Complexity Levels

- Use [EDF-0](complexity-levels.md#edf-0-rapid) for rapid, low-complexity situations.
- Use [EDF-1](complexity-levels.md#edf-1-standard) when evidence and alternatives matter.
- Use [EDF-2](complexity-levels.md#edf-2-complex) when multiple interacting origins and layered control points must be modeled.

The sequence remains the same across levels. The depth changes.

## Relationship To Clarity

EDF creates the diagnostic grammar.

Diagnostic Calibration improves confidence in the diagnostic model.

Clarity uses the calibrated understanding to evaluate decisions.

E3 [stage S1] Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
E4 [stage S1] Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
E6 [stage S1] Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.

H1: The October pay errors stem from inaccurate employee records carried over from the legacy system in the data migration.
H2: The October pay errors stem from how pay calculation rules are configured in the new payroll system.
H3: The October pay errors stem from hours or shift times recorded incorrectly in the new timesheet portal.
H4: The October pay errors stem from the interface that transmits the payment file to the bank.
H5: The October pay errors stem from a defect in the new payroll platform's software code.

R2: Malformed shift-pattern codes in migrated employee records -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
R3: PayLattice platform release 7.4 (24 Oct) -> October night premium underpayments (causes)
R4: October night premium underpayments -> Fall in voluntary night overtime cover in November (causes)

A1: Accept Ardentra's attribution: suspend the HR data team's edit rights pending a conduct review, re-cleanse and reload the full employee master data before the 24 Nov calculation, and absorb the remediation cost under clause 14.3.
A2: Before the 24 Nov calculation, have Ardentra restore NSP-02's night premium window to its parallel-run setting, verify it by re-running October in the test tenant, and pay every underpaid employee identified by recalculation through an off-cycle payment.
A3: Pause the four-on-four-off rota trial now to restore night overtime cover.

2	Title: Internal audit recalculation of October night premium for all night-working staff
3	Source: Fenmarch Internal Audit, workpaper IA-26-42, 14 Nov (document)
4	
5	Scope: all 158 staff with night hours in October, not only those who raised tickets. Timesheet hours agreed to the rostering system for 158 of 158. Expected premium follows the collective agreement: time-and-a-third for hours worked 20:00–06:00. Result: 147 underpaid, 11 paid correctly. For each of the 147, the shortfall equals 0.33 × basic hourly rate × hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00, to within £0.01. 8 of the 147 had raised no ticket. The 11 paid correctly are Kelsey Road staff rostered 22:00–06:00. Ardentra flagged list: 19 of 22 flagged night workers were underpaid (86%), against 128 of 136 unflagged (94%). The 190 flagged day workers were paid correctly. Re-run in Ardentra's test tenant (release 7.4, copy of production data) with NSP-02 window_start set to 20:00: all 158 matched expected pay.

input.brief: The October night premium shortfalls were caused by a configuration change, not by the employee data. On 22 Oct, Ardentra applied a template that moved the start of the night premium window from 20:00 to 22:00 for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The change was approved as a label fix and was not tested. The audit trail (append-only) shows this, and internal audit's recalculation matches it: all 147 underpaid staff lost exactly the premium for 20:00–22:00 hours, and the 11 staff rostered 22:00–06:00 were paid correctly. Re-running October with the 20:00 setting gave correct pay for all 158 staff. I am confident in this. Ardentra's data explanation does not hold: its own audit covered only 22 flagged staff, and the flagged staff were not more often underpaid. Do not approve Ardentra's proposal (suspending HR edit rights, cleansing data, accepting the clause 14.3 cost). Do not roll back release 7.4, which carries the November tax tables. Instead, have Ardentra restore the 20:00 window, verify it in the test tenant, and pay the affected staff off-cycle before 24 November. The fall in night overtime cover is not yet explained. The rota trial and the premium problem overlap, so do not pause the trial on current evidence. Gather overtime data first.
